description: Hook strategies, expectation alignment, pacing, and exceeding expectations

principles.rule: 90% of viewership graphs show a huge drop at the beginning because the intro fails to meet the expectations set by the title/thumbnail
principles.implication: The intro is the highest-stakes moment. It must immediately deliver on the promise.

principles.rule: Create titles, thumbnails, and intros at the SAME TIME
principles.implication: After making the title/thumbnail, ask: What reason to watch did I create? What expectations did I set? Then make the intro immediately live up to those.

principles.rule: Deliver BOTH the content and the FEELING promised by the title/thumbnail
principles.implication: An action thumbnail needs an action intro. A mystery thumbnail needs an immediate mystery setup.

principles.rule: After meeting expectations, RAISE the bar by revealing MORE than the title/thumbnail promised
principles.implication: Sets a precedent that the rest of the video is worth watching. Builds viewer confidence.

pacing_to_genre.description: Match intro pacing to the genre and thumbnail style

examples.pacing: Ultra-fast — 5 words in the first second, immediate visual payoff
examples.reference: MrBeast: train emerging, horn sounds, yelling in first 2 seconds

examples.pacing: Can be slower (22 seconds to explain), but pacing must match genre expectations
examples.reference: Frog pool video: slow explanation matched casual tone, still got 10M views

examples.pacing: Medium — establish intrigue within 5-10 seconds, build tension
examples.reference: Open with the most dramatic moment or revelation, then context

pacing_to_genre.rule: Create intros at the appropriate pacing for the genre and reflect the style seen in the thumbnail

voiceover_intros.description: Voiceovers enable strong audio AND strong visuals simultaneously
voiceover_intros.benefit: Not constrained by talking head — can show the most compelling footage while delivering the hook
voiceover_intros.rule: Use camera/visual switches every ~4 seconds to retain visual engagement

storytelling_intros.description: Present information in narrative order, not bland description
storytelling_intros.example: Instead of 'A bear killed 3 people': introduce the animal, build tension, THEN reveal the deaths
storytelling_intros.rule: Rewrite intros up to 5 times — every sentence must be as meaningful as possible

editing_enrichment.description: Pack the intro with production value
elements: Captions for emphasis (3 words or less)
Properly matched music from the first frame

exceed_expectations.description: After delivering on the promise, immediately raise the stakes
exceed_expectations.technique: Reveal additional value beyond what the title/thumbnail promised
exceed_expectations.example: MrBeast: delivered the train crash in 5 seconds, then immediately revealed additional experiments (fireworks in a house, etc.)
exceed_expectations.rule: This sets the precedent that the viewer should stay for more surprises

intro_quality.description: Score the first 30 seconds of every video

criteria.name: expectation_match
criteria.description: Does the intro immediately address the promise made by title/thumbnail?

criteria.name: feeling_match
criteria.description: Does the pacing/mood match the genre implied by the thumbnail?

criteria.name: exceed_expectations
criteria.description: Does the intro reveal MORE than what was promised?

criteria.name: visual_density
criteria.description: Are there new visuals every 4-5 seconds?

criteria.name: audio_enrichment
criteria.description: Music, SFX, voiceover quality in first 30 seconds?

criteria.name: no_filler
criteria.description: Zero wasted sentences? No 'hey guys' or 'welcome back'?

anti_patterns.mistake: Intro doesn't match the expectations set by title/thumbnail
anti_patterns.consequence: Massive early drop-off — 90% of viewership graphs show this
anti_patterns.fix: Create title, thumbnail, and intro at the same time. Ask: what did I promise?

anti_patterns.mistake: Slow intro for an action/entertainment video (or fast intro for calm genre)
anti_patterns.fix: Match pacing to genre. Action = immediate payoff. Calm = measured setup.

anti_patterns.mistake: Asking for likes/subs in the intro
anti_patterns.consequence: Breaks immersion at the most critical moment

anti_patterns.mistake: Bland descriptive opening instead of narrative storytelling
anti_patterns.consequence: No emotional hook — viewer processes information without caring
anti_patterns.fix: Present information in narrative order. Build tension before the reveal.
